task: Research with data, not product code. Write ONE new file OPPONENT_BASELINE.md at the pokerbot root answering the open decision: should the opponent model's population baseline come from the 2009 IRC poker hand-history archive (or another public corpus RESOURCES_EXPLOITATION.md names) or from observe-first play? The operator has ruled on licences: just use the code and data. DO IT WITH DATA: download the IRC archive (or the largest public no-limit corpus you can actually fetch) into the scratchpad directory, not the repository; commit a parser script under research/ that computes per-player VPIP, PFR, aggression factor, fold-to-continuation-bet and went-to-showdown, per table size 2-9; report the population distributions (median, quartiles, sample sizes) per table size, how many players have 100+ and 1,000+ hands, how long the parse took on this laptop, and the 1-minute load average beside timings. Compare with published population figures for modern online no-limit (any study or tracker-vendor report you can verify) and say plainly whether a 2009 fixed-limit-heavy corpus is a usable prior for today's no-limit games and at what shrinkage weight OPPONENT_MODEL_DESIGN.md's warm-up would need. Verify every source by visiting it. End with one recommendation and the number of observed hands after which observe-first beats the archive prior. Rate against: (a) 2-9 players, (b) true no-limit, (c) exploiting specific opponents by identity, (d) hours on one laptop, (e) fits a public GPL-3.0 repository. Do not touch any existing file. GitHub first: git fetch origin; git merge origin/main; git push -u origin <branch>; gh pr create --draft titled with the task; push as you go; end with a push. Never commit the corpus itself. Run fleet tooling from /Users/chasethompson/heater (bin/inbox.py check --summary before filing a finding). Report branch and PR URL.
done_when: OPPONENT_BASELINE.md committed and pushed with per-table-size population distributions produced by a committed parser script over a really downloaded corpus, sample sizes, parse timings with load, a comparison with a verified modern figure, and one recommendation with the crossover hand count; draft PR open; corpus not committed; no existing file touched.
